scenes.name: Sonic Youth, Swans y el regreso del ruido
scenes.book: Postpunk. Romper todo y empezar de nuevo
scenes.author: Simon Reynolds
scenes.desc: Hacia 1983 los hipsters del downtown se vuelven antibritánicos y vuelven las guitarras: unos al hardcore, otros a resucitar la no wave. El Noise Fest de Thurston Moore (White Columns, 1981) con Glenn Branca y Ut; Sonic Youth (Confusion Is Sex, 1983) y Swans forman un nuevo canon de grupos ruidosos y casi exclusivamente blancos, lejos de la pista de baile.

xref.title: Founding and Identity (1981)
xref.body: Thurston Moore (guitarist) and Kim Gordon (bass player) were founding members of Sonic Youth in 1981. Along with guitarist Lee Renaldo and drummer Steve Shelley, the band became known as the quintessential American indie rock band throughout the 1980s. "Guitarist Thurston Moore and bass player Kim Gordon were founding members of the band in 1981. Together with guitarist Lee Renaldo and drummer Steve Shelley, they made Sonic Youth into the quintessential American indie rock band throughout the 1980s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Marriage and Daughter (June 9, 1984)
xref.body: Thurston Moore and Kim Gordon married on June 9, 1984. Ten years later, they had a daughter named Coco. "Thurston and Kim got married on June 9th, 1984, and 10 years later they had a daughter named Coco."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Major Label Signing and Influence on Nirvana (1990)
xref.body: The band signed a major record deal with DGC records in 1990, which was an unexpected move for an indie rock band. This deal was significant because Kurt Cobain of Nirvana, a big fan of Sonic Youth, saw it as proof that a band could maintain creative control even on a major label, leading Nirvana to sign with DGC. Thurston Moore himself had tipped DGC off to Nirvana's existence. "Sonic Youth shocked their contemporaries by signing a major record deal with DGC records, resulting in a record called GU. And it was because of this deal that DGC also got their hands on this little band called Nirvana."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Move to DGC Records (1991)
xref.body: Facing financial constraints from Subpop despite high hopes for the band, Nirvana signed a contract with DGC on January 4, 1991. Their decision was influenced by Sonic Youth's earlier move to the same label, with Kurt Cobain believing if it was good enough for Sonic Youth, it was good enough for Nirvana. "So on January 4th, 1991, it was announced that Nirvana had signed a contract with DGC. Now why DGC? Well, like Thurston Moore said, it was because Sonic Youth had chosen that company as their major label home."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Separation and Divorce (October 14, 2011 - 2013)
xref.body: Thurston Moore and Kim Gordon announced their separation on October 14, 2011, after 27 years of marriage. The divorce was finalized in 2013, following Thurston's affair with Eva Prince, an art book dealer who was also married at the time. "But then on October 14th, 2011, Thurston and Kim announced that they were separating after 27 years of marriage. Why? Because Thurston had a fling with an art book dealer named Eva Prince."

xref.title: Post-Divorce Activities (Kim Gordon)
xref.body: Following her divorce from Thurston Moore, Kim Gordon has continued to release solo material, work on museum exhibits, and pursue interests within the fashion industry. She also authored a memoir titled "Girl in a Band." "Kim continues to release solo material, work on museum exhibits, and pursue interests in the fashion industry. She also has a memoir called Girl in a Band, which is very good if you haven't read it."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Post-Divorce Activities (Thurston Moore)
xref.body: After his divorce, Thurston Moore was last known to be living in London with Eva Prince. "Last I heard, Thurston was living in London with Prince"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Ron Ashton's Estrangement and Side Projects
xref.body: After the initial breakup of The Stooges, Ron Ashton was estranged from the group due to the "death trip" drug use. He later played in several bands that didn't achieve significant success, though one group featured Thurston Moore of Sonic Youth, Mark Arm of Mudhoney, and J Mascis of Dinosaur Jr. He also pursued acting, appearing in the original *Texas Chainsaw Massacre* (1974). "Ron Ashton played in a series of bands, none of which did much, although there was the group that featured Thurston Moore of Sonic Youth, also Mark Arm of Mudhoney and Jay Mascus of Dinosaur Jr."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's The Big Deal About The Stooges?

xref.title: Signing with DGC Records (Inspired by Sonic Youth)
xref.body: Nirvana's decision to sign with DGC Records was directly influenced by Sonic Youth's earlier deal with the label. Kurt Cobain, a devoted fan of Sonic Youth, was convinced that if they could secure creative control on a major label, Nirvana could achieve the same. Thurston Moore of Sonic Youth had also initially brought Nirvana to DGC's attention. "Kurt Cobain was a huge Sonic Youth fan and figured that, well, Sonic Youth could sign a deal like this and still retain creative control, then so could Nirvana. And it was Thurston who tipped DGC to the existence of Nirvana in the first place."
